newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Nat.Power H1 profits slip, output seen down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Nat.Power H1 profits slip, output seen down.

text.p: National Power Plc, reporting half-year profits dimmed by exceptional charges, said on Wednesday that output for the full year was likely to be 20 percent below previous levels, but overseas income would rise.
Pretax profits for the half year after exceptional items of 57 million pounds ($95.5 million) were 194 million pounds, National Power said, down from 254 million pounds previously.

The electricity generator paid out a dividend of six pence per share, up from 5.4 pence a year ago and said it would continue to deliver real dividend growth. Its shares were off nine pence to 444 pence by 0928 GMT.
National Power said increasing competition in the UK generating market had affected first half results, as well as "a significant and growing contribution from our successful overseas ventures."
These last are expected to contribute post tax income of 70 million pounds for the full year, the company said.

National Power, which was forced to sell 4,000 MegaWatt of generating capacity to comply with industry watchdog Offer requirements, said the company was changing shape to emerge as "a leading global power company."
Its British generating capacity is now around 16,000 MW and market share has slipped to 27 percent from 30 percent last year as the total market grew three percent.
Overseas investments, however, now total 900 million pounds with interests in some 7,500 MW of capacity or 3,000 MW on a net basis.
They contributed some 23 million pounds of profits in the first half, up from just six million a year ago, while development costs eased to nine million from 13 million previously.
National Power said its repositioning "means we are well placed both to compete strongly in the UK market, and to build on our material and increasingly profitable overseas business."

The company said costs associated with the payout of a one pound per share special dividend, announced with final results in May, would total around 50 million pounds and would fall in the second half of the year.
Gearing, running at 59 percent on September 30 excluding non-recourse debt from a project in Australia, is expected to fall slightly by the end of the year.
Dividend cover before exceptional items was 2.7 times and National Power said that it felt further cuts were appropriate as it committed to real dividend growth. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds Sterling)
